text:
nate: PR #8427 is ready but blocked on architecture signoff. RFC here: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/rt-128-kv-routing — can someone from arch confirm SLO impact for the fallback plan? cc @leah @sam
leah: Thanks — skimmed the RFC. Main question: will the fallback route push p99 for small requests? Need numbers to judge.
sam: Adding to arch queue. @arch-team can you take a look today? We have a canary scheduled for Thu and would like to avoid delays.
olivia: FYI QA will pause the canary until arch confirms. Also request we document the model-variant downgrade behavior in the rollout doc.
arch-team: High level looks reasonable. Two action items: 1) add microbenchmark numbers for short sequences (seq_len 32/128); 2) spell out the automatic fallback policy (max_retries, backoff, circuit-breaker conditions).
nate: Got it — I'll add the benchmark results and update the PR description. Current fallback config (runtime/configs/fallback.yaml):
```
backoff: exponential
max_retries: 2
fallback_model: bert-quant
```
Is that acceptable or should we tighten it?
leah: That helps. We'll need p95/p99 token latency at seq_len 32 and 128, and the throughput numbers for batching=1/8.
nate: I'll run the benches and post numbers by EOD. If arch can give a thumbs by tomorrow morning we can keep Thu canary.
sam: Also pinging @merge-bot to ensure the PR stays open until we get architecture_signoff.
merge-bot: PR #8427: hold placed by @sam until the architecture_signoff label is removed.
olivia: Thanks — one more ask: please include rollback triggers in the PR (suggested: error rate >0.5% OR latency increase >20% over baseline).
nate: Will add rollback triggers and AB-test/remove list to the rollout doc.
arch-team: Once you include the bench numbers and clarify the fallback details we'll provide LGTM. We'll leave a few detailed comments in the PR for Nate to address.
nate: Great, thanks everyone — I'll update the PR and ping when done.
